title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node
statement: The tree is a perfect binary tree (every internal node has two children and all leaves are on the same level). Each node has a `next` pointer, initially None. Set every node's next to the node immediately to its right on the same level (None for the rightmost). Return the root. (The checker reads each level by following next pointers.)

hints.1_question: A node's next is either its sibling (same parent) or the first child of its parent's next neighbour. Which of these links is easy to make, and which needs information from one level up?
hints.2_nudge: Process level by level using the next pointers you already built on the level above - you do not need a queue.
hints.3_big_hint: For each node cur on a level: cur.left.next = cur.right; if cur.next: cur.right.next = cur.next.left. Then move to the next level via left = left.left.
